headline: Veterans oppose House benefits bill, citing disability cuts
pages: Many military veterans are opposing a House-passed plan to revamp retirement and disability benefits, saying it threatens compensation for future veterans. The House passed two bills last week. The Major Richard Star Act, which would give full retirement and full disability pay to veterans medically retired for combat injuries before 20 years of service, passed Nov. 12 by 392 to 18. About 58,000 such veterans are affected, and the question is who pays. The other measure combines 60 veterans bills and passed by voice vote on Veterans Day.

Critics object to the Take Care of America's Veterans Act, which cuts future disability support for sleep apnea and tinnitus and raises funding fees on VA home loans. Why it matters: veterans groups say the cuts would hit those who serve in the future. Source: Idaho Capital Sun.
